**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, T4C).**

What I found:

- **§ 4.1 (p0024)** — one-year term, auto-renewing annually, terminable by *either* Party on ninety (90) days' written notice. Our exit at 90 days sits within the fallback band (60–90 days), and HDI's mirror right operates as end-of-term non-renewal on 90 days' notice, which is exactly the fallback for the Vendor side. Neither is flagged.
- **§ 4.2(a) (p0026)** — the failing term. A one-way Termination Payment payable only by the Company, equal to 50% of the preceding twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000, uncapped, triggered by any Company termination other than the § 1.6 launch failure. Against fees of 30% of monthly Net Sales over $11,000, this is many multiples of three months' fees, so it fails the fallback cap and makes our convenience right illusory.

Redline (validated `ok:true`): capped the Termination Payment at three months' fees (average monthly § 3.1 fees over the preceding twelve months) and confirmed no payment is due where we terminate under § 1.6 or for HDI's breach. I stayed at the fallback rather than deleting the payment outright because the rest of the termination architecture is already at the fallback and HDI bears the build and programming cost against a revenue share — consistent with the rule's "replace penalties with the fallback fee cap" guidance. § 4.2(c)'s eight-quarter payment schedule is untouched.
